## Motivation

Under tensor parallelism, MLA/DSA KV is replicated across attention-TP ranks. Keeping a separate HiCache host copy on every rank consumes host memory without increasing the number of reusable prefixes.

This PR connects the components from [#36800](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36800) and the integration approach from [#26691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26691) to the current HiCache transfer and completion interfaces. It stores one physical CPU KV/indexer copy and supports two restoration methods: the owner loads and broadcasts, or every GPU reads the same shared CPU allocation. The shared path avoids cache-payload broadcasts and their communication ordering requirements. Dedup remains opt-in, and broadcast remains the default restoration mode.

This follows [#43795](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43795) and [#43798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43798). File L3 and V4/Kimi extensions are outside this PR.

## Modifications

- Add `--enable-mla-hicache-host-dedup` (default off) and `--mla-hicache-host-dedup-mode broadcast|shared` (default `broadcast`), with documented configuration checks.
- **Broadcast restoration:** allocate real host buffers on the owner; other ranks keep allocation metadata without duplicate payloads. Construct allocator-only MLA pools from `MLAHostAllocation`, preserving target/draft geometry and packed DSA row widths.
- **Shared CPU restoration:** map one allocation into all local TP ranks and register each mapping with CUDA. The owner publishes its write only after D2H completes; each GPU then loads through its own physical device indices and native layer-completion events. Wait for all readers before reclaiming shared rows, and propagate allocation/transfer failures to every rank.
- **Layer-wise broadcast:** add `--enable-mla-hicache-layerwise-overlap` (default off). Pack same-layer KV/indexer payloads and group up to four ready layers to reduce broadcast submissions. Protect staging-buffer reuse and publish load completion only after the final broadcast.
- Fence transfers against KV production and previous forwards. Preserve local physical index order and skip empty GLM-5.2 indexer placeholders without skipping main KV restoration. Preserve decode CUDA graphs after shared restoration.
- Account for one physical host KV/indexer copy while retaining container memory limits, automatic-sizing headroom, and explicit ratio/size behavior.

Shared mode supports single-node CUDA MLA/DSA, TP > 1, PP = DP = attention-DP/CP = DCP = 1, the default allocator, and `direct` / `page_first_direct`. It rejects draft, mixed/state pools, disaggregated serving and L3. Shared mode uses native per-layer waits; the layer-wise-overlap flag applies to broadcast mode.

## Accuracy Tests

Focused Linux CPU regression: **102 tests passed** — pool assembly 47, dedup primitives 23, shared allocation 8, shared restoration 18, and graph selection 6. The new assembly regression covers MLA/DSA, with and without packed drafts; all four cases fail on the pre-fix builder and pass after the fix. Affected-file pre-commit checks pass. Two-GPU tests were not rerun for this constructor adaptation.

Existing GLM-5.2 TP8 model validation covers eight configurations: **384 complete answers and 192 host restores**; restored text, full token IDs and stop states match the cold requests. A further five-run shared-read check adds **144 matching answers**. The GPU component tests cover rank-local physical indices, empty indexer buffers, delayed layers/ranks, cancellation and reuse.

These model results come from the previously validated full implementation. The latest upstream constructor adaptation is checked separately by the focused regression results above; full model benchmarks were not rerun for this interface fix.

```bash
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mla_host_dedup_primitives.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_allocator.py
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_cpu.py
python test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_hicache_shared_graph_gate.py
# GPU component tests require two CUDA devices:
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mla_host_dedup_layerwise_cuda.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_shared_cpu_cuda.py
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Sufficient L2 capacity

GLM-5.2 FP8, 8×NVIDIA H20, TP8, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and sglang-kernel 0.4.9. Use L1 = 8192 tokens and host ratio = 32, keeping logical L2 capacity equal. The node-wide KV/indexer payload drops from **210.09 GB to 26.26 GB**.

Use community `benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py`: short inputs are 16×3072 tokens and long inputs are 8×6144; two rounds, append length 64 (about 80 actual tokens), output length 16, concurrency 2, request rate 64/s, seed 42. Warm up each configuration, then measure three times. Confirm real host restoration outside the timed interval. The table reports the median of three restore-round mean TTFTs, in milliseconds.

| Restoration method | Short TTFT (vs. no dedup) | Long TTFT (vs. no dedup) | Cache broadcasts / restore |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No dedup | 423.32 | 695.47 | 0 |
| Whole-load broadcast, unpacked | 442.09 (+4.43%) | 719.65 (+3.48%) | 156 |
| Whole-load broadcast, same-layer packed | 439.73 (+3.88%) | 701.77 (+0.91%) | 78 |
| Layer-wise broadcast, unpacked | 458.81 (+8.38%) | 726.50 (+4.46%) | 156 |
| Layer-wise broadcast, same-layer packed | 455.90 (+7.70%) | 724.08 (+4.11%) | 78 |
| Layer-wise broadcast, packed with four-layer groups | 442.11 (+4.44%) | 712.18 (+2.40%) | 20 |
| Shared CPU, whole-load wait (experimental control) | 430.14 (+1.61%) | 717.97 (+3.23%) | 0 |
| Shared CPU, native layer waits | 430.34 (+1.66%) | 710.56 (+2.17%) | 0 |

Shared reads have lower short-input latency here; packed whole-load broadcasting has lower long-input latency. Neither method is universally faster. Unpacked and single-layer broadcast variants, and whole-load shared waiting, are experimental controls rather than additional public flags.

A separate same-node confirmation compares two no-dedup runs, five native-shared runs, then three no-dedup runs. Shared median TTFT is **427.36 ms / 695.30 ms** for short/long inputs: +1.19% / +0.23% versus the following no-dedup controls. The small remaining differences do not establish zero overhead for every workload.

### Equal physical host memory

A separate H20-node experiment uses approximately 13.18 GB of physical KV/indexer memory and 8×6144-token sessions. No dedup uses ratio 2; shared reads use ratio 16.0546875. Both configurations warm up and run three times.

| Configuration | Restore-round hit rate, three runs | Median TTFT, ms | Two-round throughput, req/s |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| No dedup | 0% / 0% / 12.34% | 5335.75 | 0.27515 |
| Shared CPU reads | 98.71% / 98.71% / 98.71% | 733.86 | 0.41471 |

Both configurations pass 36/36 complete-answer checks. The working set exceeds ordinary host capacity but fits after dedup; the improvement comes from retaining more prefixes. This experiment uses an earlier shared-read implementation on another node, so its absolute latency is separate from the restoration-overhead table.

Profiling shows that same-layer packing reduces broadcasts from 156 to 78, and four-layer grouping reduces them to 20. Owner CPU communication submission falls from about 8.3–9.0 ms to 4.9–5.2 ms with same-layer packing. The inspected broadcast windows show no overlap with main model computation; receiver NCCL duration includes waiting and is not the net request overhead.

### Reproduce the main production configurations

The commands below cover dedup off, whole-load broadcast, four-layer-grouped layer-wise broadcast and shared reads. Unpacked, one-layer-packed and whole-load-shared controls use isolated diagnostic variants, not additional production flags.

Generate the shared public dataset once:

```python
import json
rows = [{"conversations": [
    {"from": "human", "value": f"Session {i:03d}. Marker CEDAR-{i:03d}. "
     + (f"The river crosses the stone bridge in session {i:03d}. " * 120)},
    {"from": "gpt", "value": f"Marker CEDAR-{i:03d}."},
]} for i in range(32)]
with open("glm52-public-synthetic.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(rows, f)
```

Restart a separate server per mode, keeping other arguments unchanged:

```bash
MODEL=/path/to/GLM-5.2-FP8
PORT=30000
MODE=shared  # nodup, broadcast, broadcast-layerwise, shared
FLAGS=()
case "$MODE" in
  nodup) ;;
  broadcast) FLAGS=(--enable-mla-hicache-host-dedup) ;;
  broadcast-layerwise)
    FLAGS=(--enable-mla-hicache-host-dedup --enable-mla-hicache-layerwise-overlap) ;;
  shared)
    FLAGS=(--enable-mla-hicache-host-dedup --mla-hicache-host-dedup-mode shared) ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac
OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL" --tp 8 --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" \
  --trust-remote-code --weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints \
  --enable-cache-report --enable-metrics --enable-hierarchical-cache "${FLAGS[@]}" \
  --hicache-ratio 32 --hicache-write-policy write_through \
  --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse \
  --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_sparse \
  --max-total-tokens 8192 --context-length 8192 --max-running-requests 4 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 512 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.96 --random-seed 42 --dist-timeout 120
```

Warm each workload once with four clients, then measure three times with all clients, alternating short/long order. The fresh confirmation uses the 2→5→3 stages above.

```bash
LENGTH=3072
CLIENTS=16
# Long workload: LENGTH=6144, CLIENTS=8.
CLIENTS_TO_RUN=4                 # Warm up once; then set to "$CLIENTS".
RUN=warmup                      # Formal runs: 1, 2, 3 (five for confirmation).
curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/metrics" > "$MODE-$LENGTH-$RUN-before.txt"
PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python" python benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py \
  --model-path "$MODEL" --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --api-format sglang \
  --dataset-path glm52-public-synthetic.json \
  --num-clients "$CLIENTS_TO_RUN" --request-length "$LENGTH" \
  --sub-question-input-length 64 --output-length 16 --num-rounds 2 \
  --enable-round-barrier --max-parallel 2 --request-rate 64 \
  --disable-auto-run --seed 42 --log-file "$MODE-$LENGTH-$RUN.jsonl"
curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/metrics" > "$MODE-$LENGTH-$RUN-after.txt"
```

Compare `round.round_1.average_ttft` and verify host/device counter deltas outside timing. A first-seen counter uses zero as its previous value. Combined GPU+host hit rates alone do not establish genuine L2 restoration.

| Restoration | 3072-token input | 6144-token input |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| No dedup | 445.82 | 713.58 |
| Single owner + same-layer packed broadcast | 458.57 (+2.86%) | 725.59 (+1.68%) |
| Shared CPU reads, experimental control | 453.45 (+1.71%) | 721.78 (+1.15%) |
| #42009 rotating owners, compatibility variant | 481.13 (+7.92%) | 722.93 (+1.31%) |

This compares complete implementations: ours includes same-layer packing, while #42009 uses its per-layer waiting mechanism. The differences cannot be attributed solely to owner placement. This **low-concurrency restoration** workload does not measure high-concurrency write-back/eviction pressure, and does not establish that either approach is universally faster or contradict results reported for other workloads or hardware.

A separate H20-node experiment uses approximately 13.18 GB of physical KV/indexer memory and 8×6144-token sessions. No dedup uses ratio 2; shared reads use ratio 16.0546875. Both configurations warm up and run three times.

Additional broadcast / layer-wise results on **4×NVIDIA SM103 GPUs**, using **GLM-5.1 NVFP4, TP4**.

**Setup:** BF16 KV, L1 = 8192 tokens, host ratio = 32, `direct` / `page_first_direct`, decode CUDA graphs enabled and prefill graphs disabled. PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.9. Logical L2 capacity is equal across configurations; dedup reduces the node-wide main KV/indexer host buffers from **105.05 GB to 26.26 GB (75%)**.

We used `benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py` with synthetic conversations: 16×3072-token sessions for the short workload and 8×6144 for the long workload, two rounds, append length 64, output length 16, concurrency 2, request rate 64/s, FIFO scheduling and seed 42. Each configuration was warmed up, then measured three times. All configurations restored the same amount of host cache within each workload, with zero device-cache hits during the measured runs.

The table reports the **median of three restore-round mean TTFTs**. Percentages are relative to no dedup; positive values mean higher latency.

| Restoration method | Short TTFT, ms | Long TTFT, ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| No dedup | 565.34 | 678.90 |
| Whole-load broadcast | 595.98 (+5.42%) | 700.89 (+3.24%) |
| Layer-wise broadcast, single-layer groups | 616.11 (+8.98%) | 735.65 (+8.36%) |
| Layer-wise broadcast, four-layer groups | 595.50 (+5.34%) | 693.61 (+2.17%) |

All broadcast configurations include **same-layer KV/indexer packing**. Whole-load broadcast uses `--enable-mla-hicache-host-dedup`; layer-wise broadcast additionally enables `--enable-mla-hicache-layerwise-overlap`. Four-layer grouping is the current internal default. The single-layer comparison changes only that internal default from four to one, without adding a public flag.

**Correctness:** 240 complete answers, including 120 host restores, passed exact text, output token-ID and normal-stop checks against the cold requests and no-dedup control. The CUDA layer-wise regression also passed 1 test and 3 subtests. A final no-dedup repeat differed from the initial baseline by +0.68% / +0.82% for short/long inputs.

**Conclusion:** Four-layer grouping reduces the overhead of single-layer broadcasting, but does not establish a stable advantage over whole-load broadcasting: their short-input medians are nearly identical, and the long-input samples overlap. Dedup saves 75% of host KV/indexer buffer memory here, with approximately 2–5% remaining TTFT overhead for the packed whole-load / four-layer configurations. These results support keeping layer-wise broadcast opt-in rather than claiming a general speedup. This comparison does not test shared CPU restoration or include new profiling results.

We ran an additional same-node comparison with [#42009](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42009) to compare restoration overhead when the working set fits in L2.

### Implementations compared

- **This PR's approach:** rank 0 writes and stores the host KV/indexer data, loads it to its GPU, then broadcasts it. Each DSA layer's main KV and indexer are packed together. Readiness is published after the complete restore and broadcast.
- **#42009's rotating owners:** main-KV layer buffers and nonempty indexer layer buffers are assigned to TP ranks in rotation. Each buffer's owner loads and broadcasts it, with per-layer waits allowing the model to consume restored layers individually. A layer's main KV and indexer can have different owners.
- **Shared CPU reads, experimental control:** one shared host allocation, read directly by each GPU. This is **not included in this PR's current scope**.

All three dedup approaches retain one aggregate copy of the host payload. The comparison concerns how that data is placed and restored, rather than different cache capacities.

### Setup and method

- One **8×H20** node, **GLM-5.2 FP8, TP8**; no DP/CP, speculative decoding or L3.
- L1 = **8192 tokens**, host ratio = **32**, BF16 KV, `direct` / `page_first_direct`, `write_through`; prefill graphs disabled and decode graphs enabled. L2 capacity was sufficient in every arm.
- PyTorch **2.14.1+cu130**, sglang-kernel **0.4.10**, FlashInfer **0.7.2**. All arms used `NCCL_MAX_CTAS=8` and `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`.
- Unmodified community `benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py`, with the same synthetic dataset and seed **42**: **16×3072-token** sessions for short input and **8×6144-token** sessions for long input; two rounds, appended input length **64**, output length **16**, maximum concurrency **2**, request rate **64/s**, FIFO scheduling and a round barrier.
- Start a separate server for each arm. Run correctness checks first, warm up each workload, then collect **three measurements**. Each benchmark invocation flushes the cache before its two rounds. Compare the second, restoration round; loading, compilation and warmup are excluded from timing.
- Order: no dedup → single owner → shared reads → rotating owners → no dedup. The final control checks drift; its short/long TTFT changed by **+0.48% / −0.85%** from the initial control.

For the comparison, our single-owner/shared implementations were adapted to the common base `4549937519`. The rotating arm used #42009 revision `f851b1276a` with **one uint64 pointer-index compatibility correction**; its ownership, broadcast and synchronization logic were unchanged. This is not a rerun of the latest #42009 revision.

### Results

TTFT below is the **median of three per-run restoration-round mean TTFTs**, in milliseconds. Percentages are relative to the initial no-dedup control.

| Restoration | 3072-token input | 6144-token input |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| No dedup | 445.82 | 713.58 |
| Single owner + same-layer packed broadcast | 458.57 (+2.86%) | 725.59 (+1.68%) |
| Shared CPU reads, experimental control | 453.45 (+1.71%) | 721.78 (+1.15%) |
| #42009 rotating owners, compatibility variant | 481.13 (+7.92%) | 722.93 (+1.31%) |

Each arm passed **48 complete-answer checks**, including **24 genuine host restores**, with matching text and complete output token IDs against the no-dedup control. All **30 formal samples** matched host/device-hit and effective-input counts. We checked actual host restoration separately from the benchmark's aggregate GPU/host hit rate.

All three dedup implementations reduced node-wide host KV/indexer data from **180.96 GiB to 22.62 GiB**, saving **87.5%**. These numbers count cache payloads, not process RSS.

### Interpretation

The single-owner approach was **4.69% faster for short input** and **0.37% slower for long input** than rotating owners in this test. Shared reads improved on single-owner broadcast by only **1.12% / 0.52%**. These results support keeping the current single-owner broadcast scope: substantial host-memory savings with a small restoration latency cost, without adding shared-memory mapping and reader-retirement machinery to this PR.

This compares complete implementations: ours includes same-layer packing, while #42009 uses its per-layer waiting mechanism. The differences cannot be attributed solely to owner placement. This **low-concurrency restoration** workload does not measure high-concurrency write-back/eviction pressure, and does not establish that either approach is universally faster or contradict results reported for other workloads or hardware.
